channel.title: The Dig — Error correction route
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Error correction route preset. Today’s ranked list centers on HPC-integrated quantum control and decoding, led by 2611.17652 as the main read for its FPGA real-time layer, NVQLink transport, and qLDPC decoder, with 2611.16285 and 2611.16271 as adjacent skims on multi-GPU decoder orchestration and hierarchical real-time QEC decoding, while 2611.16971 and 2611.18378 offer lower-relevance but potentially adaptable methods for low-cost error mitigation and variational-circuit trainability screening. No pay dirt today — 1 to skim.

item.title: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
item.description:
Skim review — Real-time fault-tolerant decoding requires codesigning codes, decoders, and hardware to balance sustained throughput and end-to-end readout-to-correction latency Le2e, while accounting for non-decoding transport costs (such as 3.1 μs control/communication loops or 2.944 μs link round-trips) that are commonly omitted from isolated kernel benchmarks.

Grade 0.514 · 3.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum error correction with silicon spin qubits”

Figure

Taxonomy of the real-time QEC decoding design space, organizing single-code decoders, hierarchical code decoders, and backend implementation platforms.

Asks

How do decoding algorithms, execution strategies, hierarchical code structures, and classical hardware platforms trade off accuracy, throughput, and end-to-end latency across differing qubit modalities?

But

Heterogeneous reporting across literature prevents direct cross-study comparisons; results span disparate noise models, missing power/energy measurements, and differing timing boundaries.

Tools

belief propagation (BP) · ordered statistics decoding (OSD) · Relay-BP · sliding-window decoding · hardware platforms (CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs, cryogenic)

Abstract

Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction. In this paper, we organize decoding algorithms, execution strategies, and code constructions using common classifications and examine their performance and trade-offs under the reported evaluation conditions. We distinguish decoder-level hierarchy, where multiple decoding stages or resources cooperate to decode a single code, from code-level hierarchy, where the code construction itself introduces multiple decoding levels. We first review single-code hierarchical decoders and their cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed implementations. We then study hierarchical and concatenated codes, focusing on how decoding is coordinated across code levels through hard decisions, soft reliability information, or syndrome information. We also examine how qubit modalities shape decoding workloads and timing requirements, and review how different decoding platforms meet these requirements, including central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and cryogenic platforms. By assessing design trade-offs, this paper clarifies connections across the literature and provides a shared foundation for QEC design exploration. It also identifies gaps in performance reporting and system integration to guide future research toward practical quantum error correction.

arxave:action.title: Scope QEC decoding offload to HPC

item.arxave:action: Use the decoder-level vs code-level taxonomy and latency/throughput distinctions to define interfaces and benchmarks for routing syndrome decoding from the spin-qubit control stack to HPC resources.
Ask which readout-to-correction latency and throughput targets apply to the 16+ spin-qubit system before selecting windowed/streaming or hierarchical decoder designs.
